summary.title: Writing Rust/C++ polyglot Fibonacci in main.rs
summary.body:
I wrote `polyglot/main.rs`, and it builds and runs under both commands. I tested it with N = 0, 1, 2, 3, 10, 50, 91, 100 and 200. Both versions printed the same, correct numbers each time (for example, 1, 1, 2, 3, 89 for N = 0, 1, 2, 3, 10). My test builds compiled without warnings, and I deleted the built programs afterwards.

**How the file works for both compilers:**
- The file opens with `/* /* */`. Rust lets comments sit inside other comments, so it reads this as the start of a comment that stays open. C++ doesn't allow that, so for C++ the comment closes on the same line.
- The C++ program comes next. Rust skips it because it's still inside that comment.
- After the C++ code, `#if 0` tells C++ to ignore everything up to `#endif`. The next line, `// */`, is just a one-line comment to C++, but Rust sees the `*/` and its comment ends there.
- The Rust program follows. C++ ignores it because of the `#if 0`.
- The file ends with `/* /* */`, `#endif` and `// */`. This hides the `#endif` from Rust and closes C++'s `#if 0`.

The code uses its own big-number addition rather than standard 64-bit numbers, so large N gives exact results instead of overflowing past about N = 91.
